problem.original_text: University calculus task: For f(x)=x^4-4x^2+1, find all critical points by solving f'(x)=0, classify each as local min/max using f''(x), determine global extrema on [-3,3], and plot f(x) on [-3,3] marking all critical points and extrema.
problem.normalized_text: Find critical points of f(x)=x^4-4x^2+1 by solving f'(x)=0, classify them with f''(x), determine global extrema on interval [-3,3], and produce a plot of f on [-3,3] marking critical points and extrema.

steps.title: Differentiate to obtain f'(x)
steps.explanation: Use the power rule termwise on the polynomial; polynomials are differentiable everywhere so critical points come only from f'(x)=0. This yields an algebraic equation whose real roots are candidate critical points.
checks: f' is a polynomial so differentiable for all real x

steps.title: Factor f'(x) and apply zero product property
steps.explanation: Factor common factors to reduce to simpler factors; factoring preserves roots. Apply the zero product property to find real solutions.
checks: Factors imply possible roots x=0 and x^{2}=2

steps.title: Solve factors to list critical points
steps.explanation: Solve each factor equal to zero; for x^{2}=2 include both signs for real solutions. Since derivative exists everywhere, these are all critical points.
checks: Substitute back: f'(0)=0 and f'(\pm\sqrt{2})=0

steps.title: Compute the second derivative f''(x)
steps.explanation: Differentiate f'(x) using the power rule; f'' is continuous everywhere so the second derivative test applies at the critical points.
checks: f'' is defined at all critical points

steps.title: Classify critical point at x=0 using f''
steps.explanation: Evaluate f'' at 0; sign of f'' gives concavity and thus local classification by the second derivative test (negative implies local maximum).
checks: Sign change check: f'(x) changes from positive to negative across 0 (e.g., f'(-0.1)>0, f'(0.1)<0)

steps.title: Classify critical points at x=\pm\sqrt{2} using f''
steps.explanation: Evaluate f'' at \pm\sqrt{2}; since f'' depends on x^{2} both symmetric points share the same value. Positive second derivative indicates local minima.
checks: Alternative sign check: f' changes from negative to positive at each \pm\sqrt{2}

steps.title: Evaluate f at critical points
steps.explanation: Substitute each critical point into the polynomial to obtain exact candidate extremum values for later comparison on the closed interval.
checks: Symmetry: f(-\sqrt{2})=f(\sqrt{2})

steps.title: Evaluate f at endpoints of [-3,3]
steps.explanation: By the extreme value theorem, include closed-interval endpoints as candidates; compute polynomial values exactly at x=\pm 3.
checks: Endpoint values are larger than interior critical values computed earlier

steps.title: Compare all candidate values to determine global extrema on [-3,3]
steps.explanation: List candidate values from critical points and endpoints and compare numerically; the largest is global maximum and the smallest is global minimum on the closed interval.
checks: Sanity: function is even so extrema occur symmetrically; computed values are consistent

steps.title: Specify plot recipe for visualization
steps.explanation: Provide a function_2d plotting recipe over [-3,3] with markers at critical points and endpoints; include sampling and solver tolerance but no raw data. Visualization validates classifications and locations.
checks: Plot will show local minima near x=\pm\sqrt{2} and local maximum at x=0 and larger endpoint maxima at x=\pm 3

final_answer.answer_text: Critical points: x=-\sqrt{2}, 0, +\sqrt{2}. Local maximum at x=0 with f(0)=1. Local minima at x=\pm\sqrt{2} with f(\pm\sqrt{2})=-3. On [-3,3], global maxima f(\pm3)=46 at x=\pm3; global minima f(\pm\sqrt{2})=-3 at x=\pm\sqrt{2}.
final_answer.answer_latex: Critical\ points:\ x=-\sqrt{2},\ 0,\ \sqrt{2}.\quad f''(0)=-8<0\Rightarrow\text{local max at }0,\ f(0)=1.\quad f''(\pm\sqrt{2})=16>0\Rightarrow\text{local mins at }\pm\sqrt{2},\ f(\pm\sqrt{2})=-3.\newline\text{On }[-3,3]:\ \text{global maxima }f(\pm3)=46,\ \text{global minima }f(\pm\sqrt{2})=-3.

render_hint.notes: Smooth curve with distinct markers for minima and maxima

common_mistakes: Forgetting both signs when solving x^2=2 and losing a critical point
Applying second derivative test when f''=0 without an alternative test
Neglecting endpoints when finding global extrema on a closed interval
Assuming interior extrema are global without checking endpoints
